brief: Deutsche Bank's weekly positioning update argues investor sentiment is already very cautious, which is why equities have held a tight range despite higher oil prices and rates, escalating geopolitical and trade tensions, and AI fears. This week discretionary investor equity positioning unwound sharply (-0.47sd, 19th percentile) while systematic strategies raised exposure to its highest since October 2025 (0.87sd, 88th percentile), leaving aggregate positioning only slightly above neutral (48th percentile) and AAII sentiment at its most bearish since April 2025 (5th percentile). Large-cap positioning (65th percentile) is in line with only ~10% yoy earnings growth, well short of the unfolding growth boom DB expects, and DB forecasts 30% Q3 earnings growth, noting equities have historically rallied into earnings seasons; this week's FOMC reaction matched the recent down-day/rally-next-day pattern. Sector positioning stays overweight only in Tech and Energy. Weekly fund flows show equity inflows jumping to a 3-month high ($79.3bn, led by the US) even as bond fund inflows slowed to a 5-month low and money-market funds saw $75.9bn of outflows.
